thread:
Sophie (support): FYI getting an escalation from Acme Corp — they're seeing intermittent 429s across both embeddings and chat endpoints since ~09:12 UTC. They claim they didn't change client side. :rotating_light:

Ethan (eng-sre): Can you paste the first example request body + x-request-id/headers if available? Also which region/cluster?

Sophie (support): Sent sample via DM. Region: us-west-2, cluster=dedicated-pool-3. Headers included: `x-rw-request-id: rw-req-9f3a` and `x-customer-id: cust-acme-42`. They reported peaks at 09:11:30 and 09:14:12, each spike ~20s with ~15-20% of requests returning 429.

Priya (devex): Quick checklist: 1) quota exhaustion? 2) per-customer rate limiter? 3) burst window misconfig? 4) model fallback causing cascade?

Ethan (eng-sre): I pulled logs from the gateway for `rw-req-9f3a` window. See snippet: ```json
{
  "ts":"2025-11-03T09:11:31Z",
  "request_id":"rw-req-9f3a",
  "status":429,
  "error":"rate_limited",
  "rate_policy":"token_bucket_per_customer",
  "token_bucket_remaining":0
}
```
Looks like token_bucket_remaining dropped to 0 then recovered. Need to know whether tokens are being consumed by one route/model or multiple.

Marta (product): Do we have dashboards that break down `throttle.count` by customer_id + route + model? That would help attribute. Also need alerting on sustained per-customer throttle rate > 1% for 5m.

Priya (devex): We have a Grafana dashboard `Limits / Per-Customer` that exposes `rate_limit_throttle_total{customer_id=~".*"}` and panels by `route` and `model`. But it aggregates at 1m resolution which can miss short bursts. For attribution, check the `ingress.router` logs and `executor` metrics (per-model `requests_consumed`).

Ethan (eng-sre): Pulled `ingress.router` logs for cust-acme-42 window. Summary: Embeddings route consumed ~62% of tokens during spike, chat-route ~30%, misc file-upload endpoints ~8%. Model breakdown: `embed-4-small` ~59% of token consumption, `gpt-j-16k` ~31%, fallbacks ~10%.

Sophie (support): Customer insists they did not change anything. Could this be a client-side retry storm?

Priya (devex): Check client-side `User-Agent` and `x-client-retries` headers. Also inspect `response_time` distribution — if latency spikes then retries could cause token bucket exhaustion.

Ethan (eng-sre): I queried Prometheus: `sum(rate(requests_total{customer_id="cust-acme-42"}[1m])) by (route, model)` around 09:11:00-09:16:00. See condensed output: `embeddings/embed-4-small: 420rps -> spike to 980rps for 18s`, `chat/gpt-j-16k: 210rps -> spike to 520rps for 16s`. So large short burst.

Marta (product): That correlates with token_bucket hit. If they had a burst window of 60s and token rate of 500rps then a short 900rps burst could drain tokens. Did they have a quota override?

deploy-bot: Deployment successful: rate-limiter v2.3.1 rolled back to v2.3.0 at 2025-11-03T08:50:12Z in us-west-2/dedicated-pool-3.

Ethan (eng-sre): Oof, rollback might have reverted improved burst smoothing. Need to check rollout notes. Also check if other customers on same pool saw similar blips.

Priya (devex): For triage: 1) provide customer with observed spike times + sample rw-req ids; 2) recommend client-side exponential backoff with jitter; 3) consider short-term quota bump or adjusted burst allowance; 4) set alert for per-customer throttle >1% for 1m.

Sophie (support): I replied to the customer with the sample IDs and recommended backoff. They asked for dashboard screenshots and whether billing will be affected.

billing-bot: Note: No billing overage flag triggered. Quota usage for cust-acme-42 at time of spike was 92% of monthly commit.

Marta (product): Action items: - DevEx to publish a KB article on "How to interpret 429s & tune burst behavior" with sample PromQL queries and Grafana panel examples. - SRE to check rate-limiter release notes and verify smoothing behavior. - Support to offer a temporary burst allowance WHILE we investigate.

Priya (devex): Draft KB: 
*PromQL snippets*:
```
# per-customer throttle rate over 5m
sum(increase(rate_limit_throttle_total{customer_id="cust-acme-42"}[5m]))
/ sum(increase(requests_total{customer_id="cust-acme-42"}[5m]))

# token bucket remaining over time
max_over_time(token_bucket_remaining{customer_id="cust-acme-42"}[10m])

# per-route request rate
sum(rate(requests_total{customer_id="cust-acme-42"}[1m])) by (route)
```

Ethan (eng-sre): Also include a note about short-window dashboards: use 10s scrape and 1s resolution panels for bursty customers. And add an alert rule: `expr: increase(rate_limit_throttle_total[1m]) / increase(requests_total[1m]) > 0.01`

Sophie (support): Customer replied: "Thanks, we'll add jitter and monitor. Can you temporarily lift our burst cap?"

Ethan (eng-sre): I can open a temporary override for cust-acme-42 to increase `burst_credit` by +3000 tokens for 10m. Will log the change.

Priya (devex): KB note: remind customers to include `x-rw-client-id` and `x-client-retries` headers to help attribution. Also suggest instrumenting client-side metrics export to us for deep triage.

Sophie (support): Escalation resolved? Customer accepted temporary bump and will roll out jittered backoff. Will follow up in 24h. Closing thread if no further issues. :white_check_mark:
